title.en: Parasternal short axis at mitral valve level

idea.en: Find the mitral valve midway between base and apex.

alt.en: Echo Lab render of the Parasternal short axis at mitral valve level. Learn the round ventricle with meeting leaflets at this level.

caption.en: Echo Lab render of the Parasternal short axis at mitral valve level. Learn the round ventricle with meeting leaflets at this level.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

steps.en: What you see: The left ventricle appears as a circle with the anterior and posterior mitral leaflets meeting in the middle like lips. The leaflets should be thin and swing wide open in diastole, then close fully in systole.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values and stenosis thresholds: Mitral valve area below 1.0 sq cm means severe stenosis.
Mean transmitral gradient above 10 mmHg at a normal heart rate means severe stenosis.
Valve area in sq cm equals 220 divided by the pressure half time in milliseconds.

Pitfalls: Leaflet tips look thick in a basal cut even in a normal valve, so never judge thickness away from the tips. In atrial fibrillation average gradients over at least five beats, since the gradient swings with cycle length.

Indian context: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India. Commissural fusion with a fish mouth orifice in this view is the hallmark of rheumatic mitral stenosis, and planimetry of the orifice here is the reference method for valve area.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Cutting too basal so the leaflets look thick and stenotic. Correct it by sweeping slightly toward the apex until the leaflet tips read at their thinnest.
Including papillary muscle by sitting too apical. Correct it by sweeping slightly toward the base until muscle gives way to valve tissue.
Off centre cut that overstates leaflet separation. Correct it by centring the cavity on screen and keeping the ventricle a true circle.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left sternal edge, third or fourth intercostal space, mid sweep.
Point the probe marker toward the left shoulder, about two o clock.
Sweep down from the aortic valve level until the valve gives way to plain muscle, then come back up a touch. If papillary muscle appears, you have gone too far toward the apex.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Recognise the fish mouth orifice of rheumatic stenosis.

q.en: You see papillary muscle at this level. Where is the plane?

why.en: Muscle heads mean the cut sits below the valve, so sweep toward the base.

q.en: A valve area of 0.9 sq cm with a mean gradient of 12 mmHg at sinus rhythm means what?

why.en: Both the area below 1.0 and the gradient above 10 meet severe thresholds.

q.en: Pressure half time is 220 milliseconds. What is the valve area?

why.en: Area equals 220 divided by 220, which is 1.0 sq cm.

sources: ASE 2019 guideline for the complete transthoracic examination, parasternal short axis views section.
ASE and EACVI 2017 valvular stenosis guideline, mitral stenosis section.
objectives: Find the mitral valve midway between base and apex.
Watch both leaflets meet in systole.
Recognise the fish mouth orifice of rheumatic stenosis.
